justification: Both are the same short letter on a mostly empty page. B has tighter word spacing in the justified paragraph, a serif face that reads comfortably, and a thin header rule that gives it some structure. A has wide gaps between words in the justified first line, which hurts rhythm and readability. A's text is slightly larger and more spaced, but the rivers in line 1 look worse.

A has a strong navy title band and a bold sans-serif table header, so the invoice title stands out immediately. B is elegant but its title is small and plain, which gives weaker hierarchy. A repeats the invoice number in the running header, which is slightly redundant but adds structure. The tables are similar in both. Both leave the lower page empty.

A uses ragged-right text, so word spacing stays even. B justifies a short two-line paragraph, which opens wide gaps in the first line (B1). A's navy top band gives the page an anchor, while B's thin rule is faint. Both pages are mostly empty below the text. The serif in B is pleasant, but the stretched spacing counts against it.

Design A justifies the body text and leaves wide, uneven word gaps in the parking paragraph (A1). Design B is ragged-right with even spacing, and its serif title pairs well with the body text (B1). Both place the header band and the sparse memo content the same way, and the band colour is a matter of taste.

A justifies the text, which opens wide word gaps in the first body line (A1: 'Thank you for your application...'). B is ragged-right with even spacing and is easier to read. B's navy band at the top gives the page a frame and a little identity, and its 'Page 1 of 1' footer is clearer. Both pages are mostly empty, so the difference is small.

B aligns the title, headings, body text and table on one left edge, and numbered headings give a clear hierarchy. Its calmer navy band suits a proposal. A's heading rules add clutter, and its indented body text leaves headings hanging outside the text column. A's title is also indented differently from its headings, so the left edges do not line up. B reads as cleaner and more consistent.

B fits all six sections on one page, so the document reads as a whole. Its bold sans headings stand out clearly against the serif body text. A pushes 'Next Steps' alone onto a nearly empty second page, which leaves that page unbalanced and wastes space. A's serif headings are elegant but light, and its hierarchy is weaker. B's indented body text under flush-left headings is slightly odd, but it still looks tidier overall.

A has a strong navy title band and a header band, and its content shares one left margin with the table. This gives a clear hierarchy. B's title sits outdented from the indented body, which looks misaligned. Its rule above the title is thin and the header band is missing. Both pages are mostly empty below the content. A's header repeats the invoice number twice, which is slightly redundant, but it still looks more finished.

A uses a left-aligned sans-serif with even word spacing, plus a navy top band and a 'Page 1 of 1' footer that give it a finished look. B justifies the text, which opens wide gaps between words in the first body line, and it has no band to anchor the page. Both pages are mostly empty below a short letter.

A keeps the title, headings, body text and table on one left edge, with numbered headings and even spacing between sections. The navy band is calm and the title aligns with the content. B indents the body text relative to the headings, and the title is indented differently again. The ruled dividers add clutter, and the table is indented against the left-aligned headings, so the margins feel less coherent. B's bright blue band is heavier.

A sets the text ragged-right with even word spacing, and its navy top band gives the page a little structure. B justifies the text and leaves wide gaps between words in the first paragraph (B1). Both pages are mostly empty below the short letter.

B uses left-aligned text with even word spacing and a heavier navy top band that anchors the page. A justifies a short paragraph, which opens wide gaps in the first line ('Thank you for your application...'). A's thin pale rule is weak, and its 'Page 1 of 1' footer is more fussy than B's plain '1'. Both pages are mostly empty, but B's slightly larger text and spacing read a bit more comfortably.

A sets bold geometric section headings against a serif body, so the sections are easy to tell apart. The headings sit outdented relative to the indented body, and the code blocks and callout are easy to find. B uses light-weight headings that barely stand out from the sans body text. Its content is flush left and tighter, so the headings feel weaker and the page less structured. B's navy band is fine, but A's blue band is bolder and the title is clear in both.

A fits all six sections on one page. Its bold sans headings stand out clearly against the serif body text, and the spacing between sections is even (A1). B's light serif headings are weaker, and the content spills onto a second page that holds only the 'Next Steps' heading and one line, leaving the page mostly empty and the first page bottom-heavy with blank space (B1, B2). The tables are similar in both designs.

A fits the whole proposal on one page with a consistent header band and evenly spaced section rules. B pushes the short 'Next Steps' section alone onto a nearly empty second page (B2), which leaves the first page bottom-empty and the second page unbalanced. B's serif type is elegant, but the orphaned section costs it.

B pairs a serif body with a sans title, and its text is slightly larger with better line spacing. Its justified lines have fewer wide gaps than A, whose second paragraph is badly stretched. A's body text is small and light, with wide word gaps on A1. Both pages are mostly empty, with the same navy band at the top.

A's bold, numbered sans headings stand out clearly against the serif body text, so the section structure is easy to scan. B's light-weight headings with rules above them look weak next to the body text, and its code blocks overhang the rules and text margin. A's blocks overhang slightly too, but less noticeably.

A aligns headings, body text and rules on one left edge, so the page reads as a single column. It has more room between sections, and the serif headings match the body. In B the bold headings sit at the far left while the body is indented, and the rules and code blocks end at different right edges. That leaves a ragged, misaligned look. B's blue band and bold sans headings are strong, but the layout feels less cohesive.

Both are near-identical short memos with a navy header band and mostly empty page. A uses a serif body that is darker and easier to read, with tighter justification gaps. B's light sans body is thinner and its justified second paragraph shows wide word gaps.

A's bold sans title stands out clearly against the serif body, giving a stronger hierarchy. However, its title sits at the left margin while the content is indented, so the left edges don't align. B has a consistent left edge, but its title is a light serif that barely differs from the body text. B also adds a heavy top band and a second rule, which is redundant. A's table is slightly more compact, and its right edge is a little off-margin. Overall A is a bit better on hierarchy, though only slightly.

Design A uses a serif title and body with left-aligned text and even word spacing. Design B justifies a short paragraph, which opens large gaps in the line 'Parking permits for the new building will be issued on arrival. Contact'. Both have a similar navy header band and a mostly empty page, but A reads more comfortably.

Both share the same layout. B uses a serif face with larger headings, more generous spacing between list items and sections, and a slightly larger header band, so it reads more comfortably and looks more polished. A's light sans body text is smaller and tighter. A's bold title is stronger, and its blue band is more vivid.

B aligns headings, body text and lists on a consistent left edge, with rules and code blocks closer in width and spacing. A's bold sans headings are stronger and more distinct, but they hang left of the indented body text, and the rules and code blocks end at different right edges, which looks misaligned. B's serif headings are lighter but cohesive with the body. The calls are close.

A is quieter and more refined: a serif title sits between thin rules and the table has comfortable spacing. B repeats the invoice number in a top band and again in the title banner, which is redundant and heavy. B's table sits tight against the totals line, while A spaces them better. B's title banner does give a stronger focal point, but the overall effect is clunkier.

A justifies the paragraph, which opens wide word gaps in the first line (A1) and hurts readability. B is ragged-right with even spacing and a clean serif face. B also adds a thin navy rule at the top (B1) that gives the letter some structure without clutter. Both leave most of the page empty, so the difference rests on the text setting.

A justifies the body text, which opens large word gaps and rivers, especially in the last paragraph (A1). B is ragged-right with a serif face and a steady rhythm, and its margins are slightly more generous (B1). A's sans-serif title is bolder and the header band is a stronger blue, but both pages leave most of the page empty. B reads better.

A pairs a bold sans title with a serif body and has a clean thin rule. Its table is neatly aligned with a restrained look. B's dark title band and the top header band repeat the invoice number twice, which is redundant and heavy for a short invoice. B's table and body text are equally legible, but B's left margin sits oddly against the header bands. A's body is indented relative to the title, which is slightly off, but overall A feels more refined.

Both are short letters with a lot of empty space below. B uses a serif at a larger size with looser paragraph spacing, which reads more like a formal letter and is easier to read (B1). Its thin rule is more refined than A's heavy top band, and its small page number is cleaner than A's 'Page 1 of 1' footer. A's small sans text is lighter and tighter (A1).

B fits all six sections on one page with bold numbered sans headings that are clearly distinct from the serif body. A pushes 'Next Steps' alone onto a nearly empty second page, which leaves the layout unbalanced and wastes space. A's serif headings are elegant but light, and the rules above each heading add clutter. B's page ends cleanly.

A keeps the title, table, and text on one consistent left margin, with tidy header and footer bands. B's title hangs outdented from the indented body, and its top rule runs wider than the content. The right edge is also uneven and the footer is sparse. The tables are similar in both. A also has a stray '1' numbering in its heading, which is a minor flaw.

B uses bold sans-serif numbered headings that stand out clearly from the serif body text, so the hierarchy is easier to scan. A's light serif headings are close in weight to the body and rely on thin rules to separate sections. A's rules and generous spacing look elegant, but the headings feel weak. A's code blocks and callout are slightly misaligned with the rule width, and B has the same misalignment. B is a bit more compact and consistent, and its list spacing is tighter.

A has a refined serif title, a top navy band and rule, and a clean footer. B adds a stray '1' numbering to the title and repeats it in a redundant running header ('1 Invoice INV-2026-0142'), which clutters the page. B's bold sans title is stronger, but the mixed fonts and redundant header make it less polished.

A has a clean title with a thin rule above and a simple page-number footer. Its heading is not numbered. B adds a stray '1' before the title and repeats the title in the header, with 'Invoice INV-2026-0142' appearing again in the footer, which is redundant. In A the title sits at the left margin while the body is indented, which is slightly odd. B aligns title, body and table consistently. Even so, B's redundancy costs it more than A's indent.

A uses a serif title and headings with more generous spacing between sections, rules, list items and code blocks, so it reads more calmly. B is tighter and its sans headings are light and less distinct from the body text, so the sections feel cramped. Both share the same structure and the same callout and code treatment.

B reads as cleaner: a consistent serif face, a title without the stray '1' numbering, and a simple top band with a rule. A repeats the invoice number in the header, in the title and in the footer, and the '1' before the title looks like an accidental heading number. A's bold sans title is stronger as a hierarchy cue, and its table is slightly tighter. Both leave most of the page empty, so B's lower density and cleaner header win narrowly.

Both are near-identical memos with a header band and short justified text. A's navy band is more sober and its header sits more comfortably, with larger body text and a better reading size. B's bright blue band is harsher, and its smaller, lighter serif body text is slightly less readable. Both leave most of the page empty and show justified-spacing gaps in the last paragraph.

A pairs a serif body with a geometric sans title, and the text is easier to read. Its margins are wider and the justified lines are slightly less stretched. B's light sans body is thinner and its justified lines show wider word gaps, as in the last paragraph. Both pages leave the lower portion empty, and both use a similar header band.

B has bold headings that stand out clearly from the serif body text. This gives stronger hierarchy and readability than A's light, small headings. B's indented body is offset from the headings, which looks slightly misaligned, and its code blocks hang out past the body text. A's left alignment is cleaner, but its thin headings and body text are low in contrast. B's section spacing is also a little more even, so its rhythm is better.

A uses a bold navy top band across the full width and left-aligned text with even word spacing and a clear paragraph rhythm. B justifies a very short paragraph, which opens visible gaps between words in the first line, and its thin pale rule is weaker. Both pages are mostly empty, so the difference is small.

B's bold sans-serif headings contrast clearly with its serif body text, so sections are easy to scan (B1). A's headings are light-weight and close in size to the body text, so the hierarchy is weak and the small text is harder to read (A1). B's indented body text creates a clear structure under each heading. A's table spans the full width and aligns well, but its overall hierarchy is flatter. A's navy header band looks refined, while B's bright blue band is heavier but still fits the page.

A justifies the text, which opens uneven word gaps in 'Thank you for your application...' (A1). B is ragged-right with even spacing and reads more cleanly (B1). B's navy top band anchors the page, whereas A's thin rule is faint. Both leave the page mostly empty, so the difference is small.

The two pages are nearly identical: a header band, a three-line memo block and two justified paragraphs, with the rest of the page empty. B's body serif is slightly larger and sturdier, and its navy band is calmer and more professional than A's saturated blue. B also has slightly wider text. Both justified paragraphs show a wide gap in the last paragraph's first line. The difference is small.

B aligns headings, body, lists and code blocks on a consistent left edge, and numbered headings help navigation. In A, headings sit at the far left while body text is indented, and the code blocks start further left than the text, so the alignment is ragged. A's divider rules are a nice touch, but its code blocks and callout have mismatched widths. B's flow is tidier.

B has bold numbered headings that clearly outrank the body text, and a serif body that reads well against the sans headings. A's headings are light and barely larger than the body, and its thin rules and small gray text weaken the hierarchy. A's code blocks also stick out past the text margins, while B's blocks align more cleanly.

Both are a short memo with a header band and the bottom of the page left empty. B's serif body pairs well with its bold sans title and reads comfortably, and its justified text has smaller word gaps. A's justified sans body shows wide gaps in the last paragraph, with 'Parking permits for the new building' stretched across the line. B's wider left margin lines up with the title and gives a cleaner column. A's navy band looks more restrained, but the gaps in its text count against it.

A keeps headings, body text and code blocks on one left margin, so the page reads cleanly. Its numbered headings and the title aligned with them look tidy. In B the headings hang left of the indented body, the code blocks stick out past the rules, and the rules and callout have mismatched right edges. The layout feels misaligned and the rules add clutter.

Both are short letters with nearly identical content. A adds a thin rule at the top and a 'Page 1 of 1' footer, which frame the page. A's text is slightly tighter and less stretched by justification. B's wider justified spacing gives visible gaps in the first line. A is a little more polished.

A fits everything on one page. Its bold numbered sans headings are clear and the spacing between sections is even. B spills the short 'Next Steps' section onto a mostly empty second page, which looks unbalanced and wastes space. B's light serif headings and rule dividers look elegant but give weaker hierarchy, and the small body text is harder to read. The tables are similar in both.

Design A justifies the body text, which opens wide uneven gaps between words in the last paragraph ("Parking permits for the new building..."). Design B is left-aligned, so its word spacing is even and it reads more smoothly. B's serif title also pairs well with its body face. Both use a similar dark header band and leave the lower page mostly empty, so those points are close to equal. B has slightly more generous margins and spacing.

A uses a serif title on a dark navy band that matches the serif body, so it reads as a coherent memo. Its left-aligned body has even word spacing. B justifies the text, which opens large gaps in the second paragraph ("Parking permits for the new building will be issued on arrival"), and that hurts rhythm and readability. B's sans-serif title is bold but clashes with the serif body. Both leave most of the page empty.

A uses bold, numbered section headings in a serif/sans pairing that stand out clearly from the body text (A1). B's light-weight headings are close in size to the body and rely on blue rules to separate sections, which makes the hierarchy weaker and the page busier (B1). The tables and header bands are nearly identical in both designs.

A keeps the title, bill-to line, table and totals on one left margin, and the top navy band plus rule frame the page neatly. In B the title is outdented against the indented body, and the rule and table are misaligned with the footer, so the page feels off-balance. B's bold sans title is stronger, but the mismatch with the serif body and the broken alignment cost it.

Both pages are nearly identical: a dark header band over a short memo that leaves the lower page empty. A sets the body in a refined serif with even word spacing and a serif title that matches the body. B justifies the text, which opens wide rivers in the last line of the second paragraph (B1). Its sans title also sits less coherently with the serif body.

A has a navy title band and a header band that give a clear identity and a strong title. B has a stray '1' numbering prefix on the title and repeats it in the running header, and its plain serif header looks weaker. The tables are nearly identical, and both pages leave the lower half empty.

A uses bold sans headings with numbering, which are clearly stronger than B's light serif headings. A's section spacing is compact and consistent. B adds rules above each heading, which separate sections but make the layout feel more fragmented, and its code blocks are wider than the rules and text, so the edges misalign. A has a similar slight misalignment, but its headings are easier to scan.

Design B fits all sections on one page with consistent spacing, so the document reads as a whole. Design A spills a single short 'Next Steps' section onto a nearly empty second page, which leaves a large dead area and breaks the flow. A's serif type is elegant, but its text is small and light. The headers, table and rules are otherwise very similar in the two designs.

A sets bold sans headings over a serif body, so the sections stand out clearly (A1). B uses light-weight headings that are only slightly larger than the body text, which flattens the hierarchy (B1). B aligns headings, body and table on one left edge, which is tidier. A indents the body and table relative to the headings, which looks a little uneven. A's royal-blue band is bright, while B's navy band is more restrained. Overall A is easier to scan.

B has a navy header band and a title banner with white text that give a strong, clear entry point and a more finished look. A is clean but plain, and its title has a stray '1' numbering prefix. The tables are nearly identical, and both pages leave a large blank area below the content. B's footer is slightly misaligned with its content margins, a minor flaw.

A sets the letter in a serif face with wider margins and a thin navy rule, which suits a formal letter. B uses a sans face with a thick top band that feels heavier. Both leave the page mostly empty. A's text block sits slightly better in its margins, and its small page number is less intrusive than B's 'Page 1 of 1'.

B uses bold numbered section headings with a serif body, so the sections are easy to find and scan (B1). A has light-weight headings and small sans body text; blue rules above each section add clutter and the headings barely stand out from the body (A1). Both have the same header band and a similar table, but B's spacing between sections is more even and relaxed.
